sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t
sources.locator: Section 1.3.3 'The gamma factor' pp. 25-27 (figure s and the two-leg metric computation, the reunion discussion, the time-dilation box, the operationalism passage and the symmetry/asymmetry discussion) and section 1.5 'Triangle and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities' pp. 36-37 (1.5.1 two timelike vectors and the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the note on future-directedness, figure ai; 1.5.2-1.5.3 the spacelike cases); printed page numbers as in the archived PDF text layer

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 (figure s and its computation, p. 25): the metric evaluation of the two spacetime displacements of the twin diagram, giving proper time t for the earthbound twin and t sqrt(1-v^2) for the traveling twin
contents.support: The pair's worked two-leg itinerary is the c-retained, (-+++) coordinate form of this computation with exact rationals, including both legs and the straight comparison; the source's single diagram computation is expanded into the straight value 2T and the two-leg value 2T/gamma.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 p. 25: the Lorentz factor gamma = 1/sqrt(1-v^2) and the conclusion that the earthbound twin experiences a time greater by the factor gamma; 'the same results apply for c and d'
contents.support: The thought experiment states the c-retained reading ratio 2T versus 2T/gamma for the two explicit histories and derives it from the postulates, so the source's factor-gamma conclusion is scaffolded as the scenario's quantitative clause.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 pp. 25-26: the reunion discussion ('when the astronaut twin returns home, still youthful, the earthbound twin can be old and gray'; the objection that the traveling twin could call herself at rest) and the associated figure s
contents.support: The thought experiment states the two explicit histories, the common departure and reunion events p and q, the corner r and the conditional reading comparison; the source's verbal scenario is thereby given a complete conditional deduction from the postulates.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 p. 26: 'Time dilation is symmetrical ... the asymmetry comes about because a and c are parallel, but b and d are not'
contents.support: The remark makes the asymmetry precise: the two images are not related by any affine chart transition because the traveler's image contains the non-collinear triple (p, r, q), and it records the accompanying synchronization bookkeeping for the traveler's two momentary rest frames.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 p. 26: the operationalism passage ('time is defined as what a clock measures', Bridgman) and the claim that the rates of all physical processes are affected equally
contents.reason: The framework adopts the clock hypothesis as a specified physical postulate instead of defining time operationally, and the claim that every physical process is slowed by the same factor is an additional hypothesis about all interactions, not a mathematical statement; no item of this pair adopts either, and neither is needed for the conditional comparison.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 Example 7 (Pioneer 10), p. 25: quoted telemetry positions and the numerical estimate that the spacecraft clock is 0.4 s behind the sun frame
contents.reason: A numerical estimate from quoted telemetry that tacitly treats the trajectory as one straight segment and omits gravitational and solar-system effects; the framework does not adopt secondary numerical estimates as experimental evidence, and an experiment item would need the primary report with apparatus, calibration, systematics and an uncertainty model.

contents.name: Section 1.3.4 'Length contraction' box, p. 27: the moving-rod contraction factor 1/gamma
contents.reason: Length contraction and its measuring-frame simultaneity caveat are the subject of the observer-measurements pair, which supplies the boost time/length formulas and the operational measurement theorem; nothing in the proper-time-comparison pair uses the contracted length.

contents.name: Section 1.3.4 Example 8 ('An interstellar road trip'), p. 27: the symmetric time-dilation/length-contraction account at gamma = 2
contents.reason: The road-trip computation combines time dilation with length contraction between two inertial frames and is exactly the observer-measurements pair's worked material; this pair only compares proper times of histories with common endpoints and does not need the contracted-distance account.

contents.name: Examples 9-10, pp. 28-29: the Hafele-Keating experiment, the Chou et al. 2010 atomic-clock experiment and the 1974 CERN muon experiment (gamma = 29.33; 'one part per thousand')
contents.reason: These are secondary reports of real measurements with quoted precisions; the framework requires the primary reports with apparatus, preparation, calibration, sampling and uncertainty models before any experiment item, and the experimental-interface pair is the planned home of that research queue; no numerical precision is adopted here.

contents.name: Section 1.5.1 'Two timelike vectors' pp. 36-37: the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality |m.n| >= |m||n| for timelike m,n, proved by splitting n into parallel and perpendicular parts and using the signature
contents.support: The pair supplies a complete coordinate proof in an inertial frame for future timelike vectors, including the equality case (positive proportionality) and the past-timelike clause; the source's signature-specific splitting argument is converted to the (-+++) convention with x^0 = c t.

contents.name: Section 1.5.1 p. 37: the note that the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality holds without assuming future-directedness while the reversed triangle inequality needs both vectors future-directed, with the evaluation of (m+n)^2 - (|m|+|n|)^2 assigned to problem 18 and the spacelike reversed form to problem 19
contents.support: The corollary proves the reversed triangle inequality, the convexity of the future timelike set and the finite-sum form with equality cases, so the results the source assigns to exercises are supplied completely; the exercise assignments themselves are not treated as suppliers.

contents.name: Figure ai and its caption, p. 36: |m+n| as the proper time of the spaceship that moved inertially with the earth and |m|+|n| as the greater proper time of the traveling spaceship
contents.support: The general endpoint-bound theorem with its equality case is the item that scaffolds exactly this claim for the whole approved weak piecewise-C1 future timelike class, proved locally by the improper-integrability supplier; its former corner-hypothesis (H) class remains an ordinary Riemann special case; the two-segment itinerary of the figure is its piecewise inertial special case.

contents.name: Sections 1.5.2-1.5.3 pp. 36-37: spacelike pairs not spanning the light cone obey the ordinary Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities, and spacelike pairs spanning the light cone obey a reversed form
contents.reason: These clauses concern spacelike pairs, which are not clock histories and have no proper-time comparison; the pair's scope is future timelike worldlines, and the only boundary fact it needs (failure of the reversed forms outside the same-orientation timelike class) is recorded in its companion counterexample.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (3 December 1997), complete author notes, 238 PDF pages, printed pp. 1-231
sources.locator: Chapter 3 'Curvature', section 3.3 'Geodesics' printed pp. 68-73 (PDF pages 75-80): the geodesic equation from parallel transport (3.46)-(3.47) p. 68; the proper-time functional (3.48) and its variation (3.49)-(3.56) pp. 69-70; affine parameter discussion (3.58)-(3.59) pp. 70-71; causal-character preservation, null geodesics and the maximality discussion with the 'locally' caveat and the twin remark pp. 71-72; the exponential map (3.60)-(3.61) p. 72 and its continuation p. 73

contents.name: Section 3.3 pp. 68-70: the proper-time functional (3.48), its calculus-of-variations treatment (3.49)-(3.53) and the resulting geodesic equation (3.54)-(3.56) in a general Lorentzian metric
contents.reason: The variational derivation of the geodesic equation for a general Lorentzian metric is the subject of the general-relativity connection/geodesic pages; the flat pair proves its endpoint bound and equality case directly by integration in a rest frame and does not need the variational machinery.

contents.name: Section 3.3 pp. 71-72: 'timelike geodesics ... in fact they maximize the proper time', with the jagged-null-curve heuristic and the caveat that 'maximize' should be read locally, and the observation that two geodesics between the same points can both be stationary with different lengths
contents.support: The general curved statement and its heuristic are absorbed as motivation only: the pair proves the flat global bound c Delta tau <= T with its exact equality case, and it records that curved-spacetime maximality is outside its scope rather than asserting it.

contents.name: Section 3.3 p. 72: 'This is how you can remember which twin in the twin paradox ages more — the one who stays home is basically on a geodesic, and therefore experiences more proper time'
contents.support: The thought experiment turns the mnemonic into a complete conditional deduction: the stay-at-home history is the straight inertial worldline, the traveler's two-leg history is piecewise inertial, and the readings are computed and compared at the common reunion event.

contents.name: Section 3.3 p. 72, equations (3.60)-(3.61): the exponential map defined by following the unique geodesic with given initial tangent, and its local invertibility p. 73
contents.reason: The exponential map and normal-coordinate construction are the subject of the general-relativity geodesic pages and presuppose the curved connection theory; nothing in the flat proper-time comparison uses them.

sources.locator: Section 2.3 'Curves of extremal proper time', printed pp. 28-30 (PDF pages 29-31): the extremal proper-time problem and the functional tau[lambda] (2.15)-(2.16); the Euler-Lagrange equation (2.17) and the chain of computations (2.18)-(2.25); the Minkowski example and the maximization statement on p. 30; the Lagrangian remark and exercise (2.26)

contents.name: Section 2.3 pp. 28-30: the extremal proper-time problem for timelike curves between two points, the functional tau[lambda] (2.15)-(2.16) and its Euler-Lagrange equation (2.17), and the derivation of the geodesic equation (2.22)-(2.24) with the Christoffel symbols (2.25)
contents.reason: The variational derivation of the geodesic equation in a general Lorentzian manifold is the subject of the general-relativity connection/geodesic pages; the flat endpoint bound and equality case of this pair are proved directly by integration and use no Euler-Lagrange argument.

contents.name: Section 2.3 p. 30, Minkowski example: with constant metric components in an inertial frame the geodesic equation reduces to d^2x^mu/dtau^2 = 0, so timelike curves of extremal proper time are straight lines, and 'it can be shown that these lines maximize the proper time between two points' (true only locally in a general spacetime)
contents.support: The pair proves the flat statement completely and globally: every worldline of its corner-hypothesis class satisfies c Delta tau <= T, equality holds exactly for the future-directed straight reparametrizations, and the strict case is characterized; the source's unproved 'it can be shown' clause is not treated as a proof of the local curved statement, which is outside this pair's scope.

contents.name: Section 2.3 p. 30, Remark and Exercise: the equivalent Lagrangian L = -g_{mu nu}(x) dx^mu/dtau dx^nu/dtau (2.26) as the easy route to the geodesic equation, and the remark that the same equation describes extremals in Riemannian geometry and spacelike Lorentzian curves
contents.reason: The Lagrangian shortcut is an exercise-level computational device for the curved geodesic equation, and the Riemannian/spacelike analogue is not a clock comparison; neither is needed by the flat proper-time comparison, which uses no variational principle.
